subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm examining the rendered model and noticing the head looks like a boxy helmet sitting low between oversized pauldrons, with the face plate positioned a bit awkwardly—I need to identify a few targeted fixes to improve the proportions.

Checking the halo and rod attachment, the positioning seems fine since the rod connects properly to the halo's bottom edge. The arms bend a bit oddly in the side view, and the hands look weak with thin stick-like fingers hanging from the forearm blocks—enlarging the finger radius and length could help them read as proper fists, and the pauldrons still seem oversized compared to the rest of the figure.

The pauldrons dominate the silhouette and obscure the head in three-quarter view, so I want to shrink them down and lower their vertical position slightly to improve head visibility, adjusting the spikes and flame details to match. Then there's the question of whether the head itself needs to be bigger or repositioned upward to balance against the massive body, though that would mean shifting many coordinates at once rather than a single easy fix.

Stage color's dull but fine, and the side view leans slightly lavender which reads okay. Checking the knee plates, feet spikes, and lava glow — all acceptable. The fingers need thickening though, so I'll widen them with added spike details, and the head could use a stronger brow ridge or cheek tusks to avoid looking like a plain box.

Since bone positions are rotation-only and can't translate, I'll shrink and lower the pauldrons and trapezius to visually balance proportions, and bulk up the head by adding chunky cheek blocks and a crown-like crest for more presence.

Also tweaking eye sizes and spacing so they don't overlap at the visor's center, then adjusting the pauldron array coordinates...

Adjusting spike heights and flame positions...

Now I'm enlarging the finger sweep profiles for a bulkier hand shape, and matching the thumb sweep similarly. Then I'm adding head details after the emblem line — cheek tusks, a crown, and larger back-of-head wings, plus cheek horn spikes on each side.

Finally I'm adjusting the eye line with the new lit material. Done with this pass.
